data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for the Netherlands, covering adults aged 16–65 in 2022–23. Proficiency is assessed in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—using digital tasks on tablets, with proficiency reported on 500-point scales and mapped to discrete proficiency levels. In the Netherlands, mean performance is 279 in literacy, 284 in numeracy, and 265 in adaptive problem solving, all above the OECD average, with reported shares at low and high proficiency levels (e.g., 16% at Level 1 or below in literacy; 19% at Levels 4–5). The note also reports subgroup differences (e.g., lower proficiency among older adults) and changes over time since 2011–12 (numeracy improved; literacy remained similar). It further links numeracy proficiency to employment participation and wages and relates high proficiency to well-being and civic engagement, while noting that doorstep respondents are excluded in cross-cycle comparisons to maintain comparability.
